title: Declining Mr. Litchman's offer of his own band in Washington
summary: The Washington theater owner offered to put his name in lights with his own group, but he turned it down to avoid the work of running a band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But Herman, was the pay in Philadelphia that much better than the pay in Washington? Or did you want to get out of Washington?

Well, yes. At that time it was better, but I found out later I moved too soon, because the owner of the theater in Washington, Mr. Litchman, offered me one of the best offers I think I've ever had. He wanted me to get my own group. He said I'll put your name in lights. I'll make you -- do this for you. And -- you know, when you're young, and I thought about all the heartaches and things you have going -- trying to have a band, and finding a good musician, which at that time it was too hard to find, I mean to get what you want, you know, get somebody that you could work with, that could help you along. And I said I'm tired, I don't want to teach anybody else, you know. And there's 14 15 too much work.
